scope: Encoded: s 45A(a)-(f) with s 47(c), declining where its limits cut sums credited at two rates; s 47(a)(1)-(8) and (b), (b1), (b2), (d) (refused), from 0.4.0 under a switch for the order of the deduction and the s 45A credit (fork F35), declining by default where the order changes the answer; s 40(b)(1), (1A), (1A1), (1B), (2), (3) (from 0.3.0 (2)'s second limb declined for a non-resident parent and where neither parent is entitled under (1)); ss 37, 38, 39; s 35(a)-(d) with both texts of (a)(1) selected by Amendment 262 s 2, (e) refused; s 1 'Israeli resident' (a) for an individual (a recorded finding of the centre of life, or the day-count presumptions), (a)(4) and s 14(b) refused; from 0.2.0 the second limb of s 1 'foreign resident' (its facts inputs per tax year; a resident it reaches or may reach is declined); s 1 'work income' and s 2's territorial charge and sources; s 64B(a)-(d); s 65. Inert: s 40(a) (a cross-reference to the National Insurance Law), s 40(c), s 45A(a)(2), s 47(a)(2) and (6), s 2(3), s 64B(e), s 121A (repealed). Reached and refused: the s 48 order (for s 37) and the s 48A Regulations (for ss 35, 37-39, 40(b), 45A); from 0.2.0 s 2A (an item filed under it), the s 35(e)(1) rules for one formerly an immigrant, s 66 where the caller says it governs (for s 65). Out of this row: the National Health Insurance Law and s 164 with its Regulations (each needs its own source deposit); ss 39A, 39B, 40A-40F, 41, 44-46C and 47A (outside the ruled scope); s 66 (row IL-02), s 120B (row IL-03). Tax years from 2024; the amounts ss 45A and 47 print are inputs, with the Tax Authority's 2024-2026 figures carried as published figures, not law.
tax_years_answered: from 2024; a year after 2026 on the text at retrieval (a projection)

forks.F1: s 45A(d), (e): which sums are credited when a limit cuts sums at 25% and 35%, and to which part of (e)(2)(b)(2) a survivors' sum belongs: declined where it matters. (0.2.0, D183, D187) Also computed where every creditable sum is at 25%; under (e)(2)(b)(2) the same question for a life-insurance sum; both answered where limb (1)'s fixed amount is at least what limb (2) could give under any attribution.
forks.F2: s 47(a)(7): every sum paid for him to a pension fund counts towards the 16%.
forks.F3: s 47(a)(3), (5): a negative remainder is nil.
forks.F4: s 45A(a)(1) 'אם הוא תושב ישראל': the individual must be resident.
forks.F5: s 45A(d), (e): the provisos bind only where limb (2) governs. (0.2.0, D187) Applied after the provisos: the higher of the fixed amount and limb (2) as its provisos limit it governs.
forks.F6: Insured income is taken into the qualifying work income first.
forks.F7: s 45A(d)(2)(b)(2): 'income not from work' means pension sums paid in respect of it.
forks.F8: s 47(a)(7): the exact 16% (26,436.48 for 2026), not the booklet's rounded 26,436.
forks.F9: s 45A(b1): (a)'s residence condition reaches a child's life insurance.
forks.F10: s 47(c): deducted sums come out of s 45A(b)'s pension-fund and pension-right limbs.
forks.F11: s 45A: the order of set-off against the tax is left to the composer.
forks.F12: s 40(b)(1): 'not yet 19 in the tax year' = aged 18 or less in the year.
forks.F13: s 40(b)(1A1): the election reaches (1A) points the mother takes. (0.2.0, OB1) One point moves once per child, from (1) where she also has (1B)'s (1A) points (assumed, not ruled; no total differs).
forks.F14: s 40(b)(1A): the other parent's entitlement under (1) is an input.
forks.F15: s 40(b)(1A): 'not entitled under (1)' is per child.
forks.F16: s 40(b)(1B), (2): the further point is given once.
forks.F17: s 40(b)(1B): the (1A) points are set against the tax on income from personal exertion.
forks.F18: s 40(b)(2): no residence condition. (0.3.0, O1) Declined where it matters: a non-resident parent whom (2)'s second limb would credit; 'no condition' kept as the alternative.
forks.F19: s 40(a): whether anyone is entitled to allowance points today (old NII s 109 maps to s 68 and the repealed Schedule D): an input.
forks.F20: s 37: retirement age reached in or before the tax year; an input.
forks.F21: ss 38(a), 39: the s 37 point needs the beneficiary-individual status only.
forks.F22: s 38(b): 'the said parts' are the fractional points of (a); with the income left out all of s 38's points go.
forks.F23: ss 37-39: the s 37 point is counted once.
forks.F24: s 35: calendar months, the month of immigration first.
forks.F25: s 35(c): a month abroad not left out at request uses up a month of the period.
forks.F26: s 1: no finding and no unrebutted presumption: declined, not 'not resident'.
forks.F28: s 47(b1)(2): 16% of the year's average wage.
forks.F29: s 47(b1)(2): the first 16% is counted over all deposits for him.
forks.F30: s 47(b1)(2): declined where the 12% test's two readings give different limits.
forks.F31: s 64B(b): notice by 1 October of the year before.
forks.F32: s 64B(a), (c): equal incomes give no power, as written.
forks.F33: s 65: the inheritance exception does not reach a transparent company's income.
forks.F34: s 1 'foreign resident', second limb (lines 167-169): for which tax year it deems, and whether it prevails over a centre of life in Israel: declined in the 0.2.0 form that takes the neighbouring years' facts; the 0.1.0 form answers on 'Israeli resident' alone (08i-D019).
forks.F35: s 47 and s 45A (s 47(c)): which takes a pension payment first. RULED by Meng on 2026-10-08 (SHRUG), v0.4.0: a named switch over (i) the deduction first, (ii) the credit first, (iii) the order the taxpayer chooses (an input of the reading), and the default, declined where the order changes the answer, answered where (i) and (ii) give the same deduction; each tested by name (08i-D190).
forks.F36: s 64B(d)(1) 'subject to (b)': whether a later election displaces an earlier election within its five years: declined (08i-D273); it displaces an officer's determination.
forks.F37: (0.3.0) s 40(b)(2), second limb: whether it credits the parent who shares the maintenance where the other parent is not entitled under (1) either: declined where it matters (O1 of the capstone's second independent pass).
